_comment: Hand-curated enrichments merged onto bible-wiki.json entries at load time (see loadBibleWiki in src/lib/bibleWiki.js). Keyed by entry slug. Fields: nm = name meaning; arc = story arc [{t: episode title, r: reference}]; kv = key verses worth memorizing; desc = short bio (only for entries whose generated file lacks one). This file survives build-bible-wiki.js regenerations untouched.

arc.t: Formed from the dust, given the garden

eve_1231.desc: The first woman, formed from Adam's side and named 'mother of all living'. Deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and shared it with Adam — yet the promise that her offspring would crush the serpent (Genesis 3:15) is Scripture's first glimpse of the gospel.

arc.t: Found righteous in a corrupt generation

abraham_58.nm: Hebrew avraham — 'father of a multitude' (renamed from Abram, 'exalted father')

arc.t: The offering of Isaac on Moriah

israel_682.nm: Hebrew ya'aqov — 'heel-grabber, supplanter'; renamed Israel, 'strives with God'

arc.t: Twins wrestle in the womb; the birthright bought
The dreamer in the ornate robe
Faithful in Potiphar's house — and falsely accused
From dungeon to Pharaoh's right hand
'You meant evil; God meant it for good'
Sinai — the law and the golden calf
Striking the rock; barred from the land

aaron_1.nm: Hebrew aharon — meaning uncertain, possibly 'mountain of strength'

miriam_2087.desc: Prophetess and older sister of Moses and Aaron. She watched over the infant Moses in the Nile, led Israel's women in the song of victory at the Red Sea, and later learned the cost of speaking against God's chosen leader.

joshua_1727.nm: Hebrew yehoshua — 'the LORD is salvation' (the name Jesus is its Greek form)

arc.t: Aide to Moses, spy of the land
'Choose this day whom you will serve'

rahab_2388.desc: The Canaanite woman of Jericho who hid Israel's spies and confessed the LORD as God of heaven and earth. Spared by the scarlet cord, she entered Israel — and the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1:5).

deborah_997.desc: Prophetess and judge who held court under a palm tree and summoned Barak to battle against Sisera's iron chariots. Her victory song in Judges 5 is among the oldest poetry in Scripture.

gideon_1314.nm: Hebrew gid'on — 'hewer, one who cuts down'

arc.t: Three hundred men against a multitude
The ephod that became a snare
Gleaning in the field of Boaz

hannah_1400.desc: A woman of deep grief and deeper prayer. Barren and provoked, she wept before the LORD at Shiloh and vowed her son to His service; God gave her Samuel, and her song of praise anticipates Mary's Magnificat.

samuel_2469.nm: Hebrew shemu'el — 'heard by God' or 'name of God'

arc.t: Asked of God, given back to God
Anointed the least of eight brothers
King over all Israel; the ark comes home
Absalom's rebellion and a father's grief
Last words of the sweet psalmist

goliath_1327.nm: Possibly from Lydian; the champion (Hebrew ish-habbenayim, 'man of the space between')
goliath_1327.desc: The Philistine champion of Gath, over nine feet tall, who defied the armies of the living God for forty days — and fell to a shepherd boy's sling and stone in the valley of Elah.

arc.t: A heart turned by many wives

elijah_1131.nm: Hebrew eliyyahu — 'my God is the LORD'

arc.t: The still small voice at Horeb

esther_1343.nm: Persian stara, 'star'; her Hebrew name Hadassah means 'myrtle'

job_1639.nm: Hebrew iyyov — possibly 'persecuted' or 'where is the father?'

arc.t: The LORD answers from the whirlwind

ezekiel_1237.desc: Priest and prophet of the exile, carried to Babylon in 597 BC. By the Chebar canal he saw the wheels and the glory of the LORD, acted out sieges, and promised a new heart of flesh and dry bones brought to life.

arc.t: The king's dream of the statue
Visions of the Son of Man
Prayer from the belly of the fish
The angry prophet and the plant

jesus_905.nm: Greek Iesous, from Hebrew yehoshua — 'the LORD saves' (Matthew 1:21)

arc.t: Miracles by the sea of Galilee
'Who do you say that I am?'

peter_2745.nm: Greek petros — 'rock, stone'; born Simon, renamed by Jesus

arc.t: 'Do you love me? Feed my sheep'
The vision that opened the door to the Gentiles

paul_2479.nm: Greek Paulos — 'small'; born Saul of Tarsus

arc.t: To Europe — Philippi and the jailer
Arrest in Jerusalem; appeal to Caesar

stephen_2802.desc: One of the seven chosen to serve tables, 'full of grace and power'. His defense before the council retold Israel's whole story; his stoning made him the church's first martyr — with a young man named Saul looking on.

timotheus_2863.desc: Paul's 'true child in the faith', raised on the Scriptures by his mother Eunice and grandmother Lois. Timid by temperament but steady in service, he received two of Paul's final letters and pastored in Ephesus.

lazarus_1812.nm: Greek Lazaros, from Hebrew el'azar — 'God has helped'
lazarus_1812.desc: The brother of Martha and Mary of Bethany, whom Jesus loved — and raised from the tomb after four days, the sign that sealed the plot against Jesus' own life.

martha_1937.nm: Aramaic marta — 'lady, mistress of the house'
martha_1937.desc: Hostess of Bethany, sister of Mary and Lazarus. Jesus gently corrected her anxious serving — yet it was Martha who confessed, before the tomb was opened, 'You are the Christ, the Son of God.'

mary_1943.nm: Greek Maria, from Hebrew miryam; 'Magdalene' = of Magdala

thomas_2851.desc: The apostle remembered for doubting — but also for courage ('let us also go, that we may die with him') and for the highest confession in the Gospels: 'My Lord and my God.'

andrew_264.desc: Peter's brother and the first-called of the apostles. Nearly every time Andrew appears, he is bringing someone to Jesus — his brother, a boy with loaves, and Greeks who wished to see Him.

matthew_1971.desc: The tax collector, also called Levi, who left his booth at a word to follow Jesus, hosted a banquet of sinners for Him, and wrote the Gospel that presents Jesus as Israel's Messiah and King.

mark_1679.nm: Latin Marcus; his Hebrew name was John (yochanan)
mark_1679.desc: John Mark of Jerusalem, cousin of Barnabas. He abandoned Paul's first journey and split the team over it — yet was later 'useful for ministry' (2 Timothy 4:11), and wrote the earliest Gospel from Peter's preaching.

luke_1836.desc: The beloved physician and Paul's steadfast travel companion. The only Gentile author in Scripture, he investigated everything carefully to write Luke and Acts — over a quarter of the New Testament.

nicodemus_2204.desc: The Pharisee and ruler who came to Jesus by night and heard 'you must be born again'. He later defended Jesus in the council and helped bury Him with seventy-five pounds of spices — in daylight.

zacchaeus_2961.desc: The short-statured chief tax collector of Jericho who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus — and came down to host Him, repay fourfold, and hear 'today salvation has come to this house.'

bathsheba_416.desc: Wife of Uriah the Hittite, taken by David in the sin that fractured his house. After grief upon grief she became mother of Solomon and secured his throne — and stands in the genealogy of Jesus.

delilah_1005.desc: The woman of the valley of Sorek whom the Philistine lords paid eleven hundred pieces of silver each to uncover the secret of Samson's strength. Four times she asked; the fourth time he told her everything.

hagar_1348.desc: Sarah's Egyptian servant, mother of Ishmael. Twice she fled or was cast into the wilderness, and twice God met her there — the first person in Scripture to give God a name: 'You are a God of seeing.'

abel_13.desc: The second son of Adam, a keeper of sheep whose offering God regarded — and the first man to die, murdered by his brother. 'Through his faith, though he died, he still speaks' (Hebrews 11:4).

apollos_276.desc: An eloquent Alexandrian Jew, 'competent in the Scriptures', who knew only John's baptism until Priscilla and Aquila explained the way of God more accurately. He watered what Paul planted in Corinth.

priscilla_2370.nm: Latin Priscilla — diminutive of Prisca, 'ancient, venerable'
priscilla_2370.desc: Tentmaker, teacher, and church host, always named alongside her husband Aquila — and usually first. Together they corrected the eloquent Apollos and risked their necks for Paul's life.

aquila_279.desc: A Jew of Pontus expelled from Rome with his wife Priscilla. They shared Paul's trade of tentmaking, his travels, and his gospel — hosting churches in their house in Ephesus and Rome.

cornelius_956.nm: Latin Cornelius — a Roman family name
cornelius_956.desc: A centurion of the Italian Cohort at Caesarea, devout and generous. His vision — and Peter's — opened the door of the gospel to the Gentiles: 'God shows no partiality.'

lydia_1837.desc: A seller of purple goods from Thyatira, worshiping God by the river at Philippi. The Lord opened her heart to Paul's message, and her household became Europe's first recorded church.

naaman_2122.desc: Commander of Syria's army, mighty and leprous. A captive Israelite girl pointed him to the prophet; seven humbling dips in the Jordan made his flesh like a little child's — and his heart like one too.

jael_689.desc: Wife of Heber the Kenite, who received the fleeing general Sisera with milk and a rug — and fulfilled Deborah's prophecy that the LORD would sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.

zipporah_3095.desc: Daughter of the priest of Midian, given to Moses in his exile. She acted decisively at the lodging place on the way to Egypt, and bore Moses two sons, Gershom and Eliezer.

enoch_1192.desc: The seventh from Adam, who 'walked with God, and he was not, for God took him' — one of only two people in Scripture who did not see death. Father of Methuselah, the longest-lived man.

melchisedec_1991.desc: King of Salem and priest of God Most High, who met Abraham with bread and wine and blessed him. Psalm 110 and Hebrews make him the pattern of a priesthood greater than Levi's — a priest forever.

babylon.nm: Akkadian bab-ilu — 'gate of the god'; Hebrew bavel echoes balal, 'confused'

zion.nm: Hebrew tsiyyon — meaning uncertain; the fortress hill of Jerusalem
